title: Crypto trend system (daily DI + Supertrend): 8-year backtest, 100+ failed ideas, bot running on demo. Looking for criticism.
author: lks777
selftext:
Hi all. I've been building a crypto trend-following system, testing it on data, and running a bot on a DEMO account. Here's what it does, the numbers, what did NOT work, and where I think it's weak. Criticism welcome, especially on methodology.



Everything is in R (1R = amount risked per trade). "Ratio" = total profit ÷ max drawdown, both in R.



The system

Data: Binance spot candles (official history), 2018 → Oct 2026. Costs: 0.3 % round trip + 0.01 % funding every 8h, always paid.

Strategy 1, DI (long only): bullish DI+/DI− (14) cross on the daily chart, checked at every 8h close (the running daily candle is rebuilt with no look-ahead). First signal of the day only, and only if yesterday's low is below the close.

Stop: lowest low of the whole previous bearish DI phase − 0.5 daily ATR (median distance 14–19 %).

Stop to breakeven at +1R. Full exit when the daily DI crosses back. No targets.

0.5 % risk; max 4 positions at risk, 7 total (breakeven ones don't count).

Strategy 2, Supertrend 8h (long and short): ATR 16 × 2.4. Longs only above EMA 50, shorts only below. Stop fixed at the line on entry; exit when the line flips. 0.25 % risk; separate book (max 4).

Strategy 3: shorts on 4h breaks of 3-touch support lines with a bearish weekly DI. Small; adds almost nothing.

Coins: BTC, ETH, SOL, RUNE, NEAR, UNI, DOGE.

Backtest results

Configuration	Ratio, 7 coins	Ratio, 15 test coins

Initial DI (prior-candle stop, with bounces)	27.7	7.7

DI without bounces	29.4	7.8

DI with phase stop	35.4	9.0

DI + Supertrend at 50 % (current)	41.7	11.6

Current (7 coins): +615R over 107 months, max drawdown 14.7R, 1,414 trades.

By year: 2018 +6 · 2019 +44 · 2020 +61 · 2021 +220 · 2022 +1 · 2023 +96 · 2024 +148 · 2025 +8 · 2026 (to Oct) +31.

Median month +0.8R; \~44 % losing months; worst month −7.2R. The 10 best months are 69 % of the total.

Without the best 5 / 10 / 20 trades: +452 / +349 / +238R.

Monthly bootstrap: \~2.7 % of years negative.

Per-coin costs estimated from order books: no meaningful change. 14 collapsed or delisted coins (LUNA, FTT…): ratio 5.5, but negative since 2022.

Buy and hold the 7 coins: +39 %/yr with an −88 % drawdown.

Where it loses and where it wins (DI trades)

Stops: 15 % of trades, −59R.

Near-zero exits (−0.5 to +0.5R): 67 % of trades, −64R. This is the main leak: the DI crosses and flips back quickly.

\+0.5 to +3R: 11 %, +84R.

\+3R or more: only 8 % of trades, but +487R. These winners peak at +17.5R on average and bank +11R, giving back 37 % of the peak.

Weaker since 2022 in both coin lists: stop more than 20 % away, daily ADX > 30, coin more than 70 % below its 1-year high.

What did NOT work (all tested against random controls)

Entry confirmations (break of signal high, waiting for a pullback, higher low, scaling in).

Time stops, tighter stops (micro-structure) and moving the breakeven (none, +1.5R, +2R, +3R).

Cutting big winners: a "give-back cap" after +8/12/15/20R is always worse.

Regime filters (BTC vs 200-day MA, market breadth): the best months start while the regime still looks bad.

Martingale, averaging down, pyramiding. Latest one: a "ladder" buying 5–12 % dips on 8h/4h while the weekly DI is bullish, with equal or 1-2-4-8 sizing. Slightly positive on its own, but it lowers the portfolio ratio in every version (simply raising base risk is better).

Other timeframes, ICT (FVG, ORB, CRT), Squeeze, VWAP, moving-average crosses (260 combos), Fibonacci time, DI shorts.

Choosing coins by past performance.

Lesson: the best trades take off right after the signal; any waiting or early cutting makes it worse.



The test that worries me most

I fixed a NEW list of 15 coins before looking (AAVE, ALGO, XTZ, IOTA, ZIL, QTUM, BAT, COMP, SNX, CRV, SUSHI, YFI, EGLD, INJ, KSM). Result: ratio 1.9. It makes +135R in 2018–21, +4R from 2022 to Oct 2025, and has a 73R drawdown. Most of these are alts that have been bleeding for years. My take: the 41.7 on my 7 coins is optimistic because I picked them knowing they had gone up. On unknown coins the system can go flat for years.



The bot

Python + ccxt. Signals from Binance spot data, orders on BingX perpetuals, on a DEMO account, running on a small cloud server (systemd).

Safety: state saved right after every order (so a failure can't cause repeat buys); if the stop isn't accepted after 3 tries, the position is closed; a watchdog checks every 5 minutes that every position has its stop and re-places it if missing.

Leverage is only margin: 2× if the stop is ≤ 30 % away, 1× if further. Risk is set by size (risk ÷ stop distance).

Checked against the backtest: same signals and same stops. First demo trade done; \~0.5 % slippage vs the Binance close.

Plan: several weeks on demo, then real money at 0.5 % risk.

Questions

Do you see any methodology mistake (look-ahead, survivorship, overfitting) I'm missing?

How would you attack the near-zero-exit leak without delaying entries? Confirmations already failed.

How would you pick coins with a fixed rule, given the system hasn't made money on "dead" alts since 2022?

Does running something uncorrelated in parallel make sense (funding-rate carry, relative-strength rotation…)? Any real experience?

Differences you've seen between backtest and live on BingX or other perp exchanges?

Thanks for reading. Happy to share details of any test.

comments.author: Careless-Rent-4903
comments.body: I'd leave the near-zero exits alone for now, thats pretty normal for trend following. The bigger question is coin selection. A vectorbt pro run with a monthly universe picked by trailing liquidity including delisted coins would tell you more than another exit tweak. Also test fills on BingX perp data since matching signals on Binance spot doesnt mean matching execution.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Respect for fixing a new coin list before looking and then posting the bad result. I'd treat that list as your real number and the seven coins as the best case, since you picked them knowing they went up. For coin choice I'd use a rule that only uses data from that day, like the top coins by volume at each point in time, and keep the ones that later died in the test. On the near-zero exits, since waiting and cutting both failed, I'd look at whether those quick flips cluster in certain conditions before changing the rule itself. For the carry idea, it does move differently from trend, though funding can flip sign fast. If you want to compare funding across venues, Cymetica's Funding Rate Radar shows it normalised to 8h and annualised.
